gpt.rationale: For nonpayment of rent, a residential tenant is guilty of unlawful detainer only after defaulting in rent and failing to pay within three days after service of a written notice requiring payment or possession. The three-day period excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and other judicial holidays.

gemini.rationale: A landlord must provide a tenant with a written three-day notice demanding payment of the overdue rent or possession of the property. An eviction action for nonpayment may only be filed after the tenant has failed to comply within this three-day period.

pay_or_quit.description: Nonpayment of rent — CCP §1161(2). Notice demands only unpaid rent; no late fees, utilities, or other charges permitted.

mandatory_content.note: REVISED-3 (self-critique 2026-07-01): CCP §1161(2) requires name, telephone number, and address of payee. Strict compliance — omission of any element is fatal to notice. See Lynch & Freytag v. Cooper (1990) 218 Cal.App.3d 603; Eshagian v. Cepeda (2025). REVISED-8 (encoding fix 2026-07-02): Added days_hours_for_in_person_payment requirement per CCP §1161(2).

days_hours_for_in_person_payment.content: usual days and hours landlord available to receive payment at stated address
days_hours_for_in_person_payment.source_anchor: CCP §1161(2): 'if the address at which rent may be paid is set forth in the notice, the notice shall also set forth the usual days and hours that the landlord is available at such address to receive payment' — omission is fatal under strict compliance
days_hours_for_in_person_payment.note: REVISED-8 (encoding fix 2026-07-02, B-02 correction): Omission of usual days/hours is fatal under strict compliance. Confirmed by golden-set CA-NOT-B-02 miss analysis.

tenancy_over_1yr.note: REVISED-7 (self-critique 2026-07-01): corrected from calendar_days to calendar_days_excluding_weekends_holidays per CCP §1161 (SB 611, operative 2/1/2025). Court days apply regardless of tenancy length.

cure_or_quit.description: Curable lease violation — CCP §1161(3). Use only for CURABLE covenant breaches. Includes unauthorized assignment/subletting (tenant has statutory right to remove subtenant within 3 court days per CCP §1161(3)). For incurable conduct (waste, nuisance, unlawful use) use unconditional_quit (CCP §1161(4)).
bright_line_qualifying_conduct: Failure to maintain premises per lease covenant
Unauthorized pet (where lease prohibits — if curable by removal)
Failure to obtain renter's insurance per lease covenant
Failure to pay utilities required under lease
Unauthorized occupant (where lease limits occupants — if curable by removal)
Lease covenant breach capable of being remedied within 3 court days
Unauthorized assignment or subletting contrary to lease covenants (CCP §1161(3) — express statutory curable breach; tenant has right to remove subtenant/assignee within 3 court days)
cure_or_quit.note: CCP §1161(3): curable covenant violations only. Tenant has 3 court days to cure or surrender. If conduct 'cannot afterward be performed' per the statute, §1161(3) still permits notice but no cure opportunity — treat as escalating to §1161(4) analysis. See interaction gate: cure_or_quit_vs_unconditional_quit. REVISED-9 (encoding fix 2026-07-02, B-09 correction): Added unauthorized assignment/subletting as curable breach per CCP §1161(3), which expressly names 'covenant not to assign or sublet' as performable within 3 days. §1161(4) enumerated categories (nuisance, waste, unlawful use) do NOT include subletting — using unconditional_quit for subletting is a B2 HIGH error.

unconditional_quit.description: Incurable conduct (waste, nuisance, unlawful use) — CCP §1161(4). No right to cure. NOTE: unauthorized assignment/subletting is a CURABLE breach under CCP §1161(3), not §1161(4).
bright_line_qualifying_conduct: Physical waste (damage to premises contrary to lease conditions/covenants)
Nuisance (maintaining, committing, or permitting nuisance on demised premises)
Criminal street gang activity per Civ. Code §3486(c)
open_textured_conduct: Repeated disturbances or noise complaints (may rise to nuisance — fact-specific)
Unauthorized smoking / vaping (may constitute waste or nuisance — context-dependent)
Repeated lease violations that individually are curable but pattern amounts to incurable breach
Chronic late payment (may constitute waste of lessor's interest — contested)
unconditional_quit.note: REVISED-6 (self-critique 2026-07-01) + BRIGHT-LINE ENCODED (Andy ratification 2026-07-01): §1161(4) — waste, nuisance, unlawful use. No cure right. Ambiguous conduct (see open_textured_conduct) routes to open-textured analysis. Cross-refs: Civ. Code §3482.8, §3485(c), §3486(c) define statutory nuisance categories. Source: CCP §1161(4) (Justia 2025 text confirmed). REVISED-9 (encoding fix 2026-07-02, B-09 correction): Removed unauthorized assignment/subletting from this category — per CCP §1161(3) subletting is a curable lease covenant breach; §1161(4) enumerated categories do NOT include subletting. Moved to cure_or_quit.bright_line_qualifying_conduct.

federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)
federal.threshold_formula: 130% of BAH for military member pay grade E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area in the United States (adjusted annually by DoD)
federal._preliminary_threshold_was: 4073.16 (2024 — old CPI formula, now superseded by BAH formula per FY23 NDAA)

machine_verified_cases.controlling_quote: The principal issue which confronts us is this: In an unlawful detainer action, where the affirmative defense of retaliatory eviction is asserted pursuant to Civil Code section 1942.5, who has the burden of proving what? We hold that under that section, (1) the tenant has the overall burden of persuasion on the issue of retaliatory eviction, but (2) in certain circumstances, hereinafter specified, the landlord has the burden of giving notice of, and of proving, a valid ground for his action.
machine_verified_cases.holding_summary: Clarified the burden of proof under the retaliatory eviction statute (Civ. Code § 1942.5), holding that the tenant must first prove a protected act, after which the burden shifts to the landlord to show a legitimate, non-retaliatory reason for the eviction.
